subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw support cross-machine Chrome extension browser control again, and if so should it be restored as a first-party relay or exposed through a vetted browser-backend Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: This changes browser-control authority over signed-in sessions, remote gateways, CDP/debugger access, and public config/plugin contracts, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term security and product boundary.

options.title: Design a vetted backend seam
options.body: Add a versioned browser-backend Plugin SDK/registry contract and use it to support an optional relay implementation with explicit auth, scope, audit, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Restore a first-party optional relay
options.body: Bring back the extension driver and relay as a bundled opt-in feature, accepting core ownership of its browser-control and packaging security surface.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Close the workflow direction after documenting that remote browser control must use node-host or raw remote CDP paths, even though managed-hosting users lose the one-click extension flow.

recommendation.title: Design a vetted backend seam
recommendation.body: Add a versioned browser-backend Plugin SDK/registry contract and use it to support an optional relay implementation with explicit auth, scope, audit, docs, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the strongest recent history on the relay removal and browser-driver migration surface.
